Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode until we open the call for questions. Following today's prepared remarks, we will conduct a Q&A session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and company when prompted. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. There will be a brief pause prior to each question. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics', or GAD's, Q4 and full-year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today from the executive team are David Harlan, our Chief Executive Officer; Rebecca Singh, Chief Financial Officer; Thomas Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Nadia Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and James Whitaker, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we dive in, I'd like to remind everyone that today's call, including the Q&A portion, may include forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results could differ materially due to factors discussed in our SEC filings, including our most recent 10-K and 10-Q. We undertake no obligation to update these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David.

David Harlan:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a strong performance in Q4 and throughout fiscal 2023, underscoring the durability of our business model and the breadth of our diversified portfolio spanning commercial aerospace, defense, and services. We're executing sharply on our strategic priorities: advancing operational excellence, innovating across our technology roadmap, and creating sustained value for shareholders amid a favorable industry backdrop.

Today, we'll touch on key areas including our revenue performance across segments, updates on major programs, potential risks and opportunities ahead, backlog expansion, the drivers and headwinds shaping our top line, and the standout results from our priority defense initiatives. We're especially enthusiastic about progress on our Next-Generation Air Dominance, or NGAD, family of systems and its transformative potential for long-term growth. Demand remains robust for our defense platforms, while commercial aerospace continues its steady post-pandemic rebound, supported by rising flight hours and OEM ramps.

With that overview, I'll now hand it over to Rebecca to walk through the financial details and expand on these highlights.

Rebecca Singh:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with the numbers. For the full year 2023, we posted consolidated revenue of $26.4 billion, a healthy 18% increase year-over-year, propelled by strong aftermarket recovery in commercial aviation, reliable execution on defense contracts, and record services backlog heading into 2024. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $7.45, surpassing the midpoint of our guidance range, as segment margins improved thanks to an optimal product mix and productivity enhancements from our Enterprise Digital Transformation efforts.

Breaking it down by segment, commercial aerospace led the way with $11.2 billion in revenue, up an impressive 32% from last year and accounting for 42% of our total. This exceeded our projections, driven by faster production scaling and original equipment manufacturer wins as air travel demand surges post-pandemic. Narrowbody aircraft were the highlight—our GAD-400 and GAD-500 series, which compete directly with the Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo, achieved 285 deliveries in 2023 compared to 210 in 2022, with major low-cost carriers like Southwest Airlines and Ryanair converting backlog orders. By Q4, we reached 45 deliveries per month, up from 32 a year earlier, as challenges with titanium forgings and CFM LEAP-1 engine modules eased following disruptions from the Ukraine conflict.

Geographically, North America drove 55% of sales, including a 40% increase in GAD-400 units to Delta Air Lines and United Airlines for fleet renewals. Europe expanded 45% on replacements for A320neo fleets, and Asia-Pacific jumped 60%, highlighted by IndiGo's commitment for 120 GAD-500s and rebounding Chinese domestic flights despite ongoing COVID measures. Widebody results were more moderate at 15% growth to $2.8 billion, affected by delays in Boeing's 777X certification impacting our GAD-900 extended-range variant, though we're addressing this through 787-10 retrofit solutions. Emerging trends like greater use of sustainable aviation fuel are gaining traction—our advanced winglets with hybrid-electric features now support 20% SAF blends, aligning with IATA's net-zero targets by 2050. We're committing $1.2 billion to additive manufacturing for nacelle parts, aiming for 15% cost reductions by 2025, while our digital twin technology cut engineering changes by 28% this year.

Defense revenue climbed to $12.1 billion, a steady 7% rise year-over-year and 46% of our mix, reflecting precise delivery against a $52 billion funded backlog with a book-to-bill of 1.1 times. Fixed-wing efforts contributed 60% of the gains, led by the GAD Eagle II fifth-generation stealth fighter—similar to the F-35—where we delivered 18 aircraft across Lots 15 through 17 to the U.S. Air Force under the Joint Strike Fighter successor agreement, alongside Foreign Military Sales clearance for 24 units to Poland as NATO bolsters its eastern defenses. Hypersonics provided momentum, with our HAWC-inspired boost-glide vehicle moving to low-rate initial production and capturing $850 million in Department of Defense funding for fiscal 2024.

Missiles and space grew 12% together: the GAD Viper air-to-air missile produced 1,200 units to back Ukraine support through Presidential Drawdown Authority, and our small satellite constellation for the Space Development Agency's Tranche 2 Transport Layer launched 48 vehicles via SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. U.S. government business made up 72% of sales, steady year-over-year but with better cash from Cooperative Research and Development Agreement reimbursements; international sales rose 18% on Middle East needs, including $1.4 billion from Saudi Arabia for GAD Patriot GEM-T enhancements and UAE MQ-9 Reaper maintenance. Intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance faced some setbacks from chip shortages, but our C4ISR digital infrastructure with AI sensor fusion is speeding Technology Readiness Level 9 transitions. Margins rose 120 basis points to 11.8% from production learning curves and University Affiliated Research Center growth. Forward, tensions in Ukraine, the Red Sea, and Taiwan Strait support our $120 billion five-year opportunity pipeline, with fiscal 2024 outlook at 9 to 11% growth.

Services, our top-margin area at 22.4% operating margins, generated $3.1 billion, up 22% and 12% of total revenue. This stemmed from 25% higher global flight hours per Cirium metrics as carriers prolong aircraft life amid OEM delays. Engine maintenance, repair, and overhaul soared 35% to $1.4 billion, with GAD LeapCore modules equivalent to LEAP-1A/1B seeing 15% more visits on A320neo and 737 MAX operators; our facilities in Singapore and San Antonio ran at 95% utilization. Component aftermarket advanced 18%, aided by the GAD Sentinel platform's machine learning that reduced unplanned removals by 22%. Asia-Pacific topped with 30% growth on ANA and Air China pacts, Europe 25% through our Lufthansa Technik joint venture, and Middle East/North Africa 40% from Etihad widebody work. We're expanding TrueChoice long-term power-by-the-hour agreements, adding $2.5 billion to backlog, and testing hydrogen fuel cells for eVTOL with Joby Aviation partners. Vertical integration in composites has secured 40% of our parts supply.

Overall, this segment balance—commercial surge, defense steadiness, services recurrence—yielded $3.8 billion in free cash flow, funding $1.5 billion share repurchases and a 25% dividend increase. We're set for $28 to $29 billion in 2024 revenue, 8 to 10% organic growth, leveraging Boeing scrutiny and the DoD's $850 billion budget.

Gross margins stood at 22.5%, operating income at $4.1 billion, and free cash flow at $3.8 billion. Our balance sheet is robust with $5.2 billion in cash equivalents, and full-year guidance holds firm. We're optimizing costs while funding high-return growth areas and returning capital via dividends and buybacks.

Turning to backlog, it reached a record $145 billion at year-end, up $20 billion or 16% sequentially and 22% year-over-year, our eighth straight quarter of double-digit expansion. This reflects strong demand in fighter sustainment, hypersonics, missile defense, and next-gen space. Funded backlog is $52 billion, or 36%, with book-to-bill at 1.3 times on $25 billion new awards.

By segment: Aeronautics at 47%, $68 billion up 14% sequentially from F-35 Lot 16 wings worth $1.8 billion and NGAD prototypes; Missiles at 28%, $40 billion up 20% on $1.2 billion hypersonic IDIQ and $700 million SM-6; Space at 25%, $37 billion up 15% from SDA Tranche 2 and NSSL pursuits. U.S. DoD was 72% of bookings, international 28% with Middle East and Indo-Pacific strength. This provides 3.8 times trailing revenue visibility through 2026, with 60-70% of 2025 already secured.

On revenue drivers and headwinds for Q4, we hit $7.2 billion total, up 12% year-over-year. Defense at 55% drove 15% growth to $4 billion via F-35 subsystems (28 delivered) and hypersonics ($450 million), aided by NDAA supplementals. Commercial at 35% grew 9% to $2.5 billion on nacelle/thrust reverser ramps and 787 composites; services up 18% to $720 million on PHM analytics. North America 65%, Europe 20%, Asia 10% up 25%, Middle East 5%.

Headwinds included supply chain issues trimming 3 points—titanium up 25-30%—labor inflation at 7%, and certification delays shifting $150 million. We're countering with $250 million in additive manufacturing, SwarmSync autonomy ($600 million Navy award), and reshoring.

Regarding risks and opportunities, global defense spend hit $2.24 trillion per SIPRI, up 6.8%, growing 3.5% CAGR to 2028. Opportunities: hypersonics GPI $1.2 billion MDA IDIQ; NATO Tempest $450 million; Asia F-15 upgrades; 777X wings $3.5 billion; C4ISR $900 million NGA; MQ-Next $50 billion TAM. Expect 8-10% FY24 growth, margins to 12.5%.

Risks like titanium inflation (mitigated by multi-sourcing, $200 million AM), fixed-price overruns (digital twins cap <5%), macro pressures, China competition, addressed by $1.2 billion capex, hedging.

Finally, priority defense programs generated $2.8 billion in Q4, up 18%, 62% of segment, margins 14.2%. F-35 $1.1 billion, 28 deliveries, Block 4 AI fusion; hypersonics $450 million, ARRW tests Mach 5+; precision strike $650 million JASSM/LRASM 120/month; OPIR PDR $350 million. Backlog $152 billion total. Regional DoD 72%, international 28% FMS $1.2 billion.

This positions us strongly in the $1 trillion A&D market.

Thomas Reilly:
Thank you, Rebecca. From an operational standpoint, we've made meaningful progress in supply chain oversight, ramping output on critical programs. Investments in automation, digital tools, and strategic stockpiling—like localizing 40% of subsystems—have cut delays 22% year-over-year. Deliveries reached 156 platforms and 450 effectors in Q4, aligning with 15% growth targets. Our A&D Secure Supply initiative counters tariffs and rare earth risks effectively.

Dr. Nadia Patel:
Thank you, Thomas. Technologically, we're advancing next-gen propulsion and beyond. NGAD EMD hit critical design review early via MBSE, reducing weight 8%; HACM flight test #4 achieved Mach 5+; MQ-Next 150+ autonomous hours; Vulcan Centaur 100% success. AI/ML predictive maintenance cuts downtime 30%, giving us a clear edge.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to register a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Josh Klein with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Klein:
Good morning, team. Thanks for the details. Can you provide more color on the commercial aerospace recovery, particularly widebody and Asia-Pacific trends?

David Harlan:
Certainly, Josh. As Rebecca outlined, commercial was a bright spot with 32% growth, narrowbodies leading via GAD-400/500 ramps to 45 per month. Widebody grew more modestly at 15% due to 777X delays, but 787 retrofits help. Asia-Pacific exploded 60% on IndiGo and China rebound, with SAF winglets and digital twins enhancing our position. Supply easing post-Ukraine supports continued momentum.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Hi, everyone. Curious about backlog growth specifics— what drove the sequential jump and book-to-bill outlook?

Rebecca Singh:
Maria, great question. The $20 billion sequential rise to $145 billion came from $25 billion awards: Aeronautics F-35/NGAD $1.8 billion plus international FMS; Missiles hypersonic/SM-6 $1.9 billion; Space SDA/NSSL $1.1 billion. Book-to-bill 1.3x, targeting 1.2x for FY24, with international up to 28%. Exceptional visibility at 3.8x revenue.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks. Regarding hypersonics programs, any updates on risks like supply chain or testing milestones?

Dr. Nadia Patel:
Alex, happy to address. Hypersonics shone with HACM end-to-end test #4 hitting Mach 5+ accuracy, ARRW derivatives $2.1 billion IDIQ, production doubled to 180/year. Supply risks like rare earths mitigated by Australian dual-sourcing and AM cost cuts 18%. Backlog $6.5 billion, 25% CAGR potential on $13 billion DoD budget.

David Harlan:
Thank you all for the thoughtful questions. To close, I'm highly confident in GAD's trajectory to navigate macro dynamics and unlock shareholder value. Our emphasis on strategy, operations, and innovation remains unwavering.

Emily Carter:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q4 2023 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
